question: A byke travels 80 km at the speed of 40 km/hr and the next 30 km at the speed of 10 km/hr. What is its average speed (in km/hr)?
solution:
` [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = 80 + 30 = 110 km

Time = 80/40 + 30/10 = 2 + 3 = 5 hours

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

= 110 ÷ 5

**∴ Answer = 22 km/hr**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance 1 = 80 km, Speed 1 = 40 km/hr; Distance 2 = 30 km, Speed 2 = 10 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Time for first part = 80 ÷ 40 = 2 hours

⇒ Time for second part = 30 ÷ 10 = 3 hours

⇒ Total time = 2 + 3 = 5 hours

⇒ Total distance = 80 + 30 = 110 km

⇒ Average speed = 110 ÷ 5

⇒ = 22 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 22 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed Formula

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

Important Note

Do not take simple average of speeds unless time is equal

Time Calculation

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Shortcut Insight

Always convert into time first, then apply formula
